annotation.method: Codex read the complete 24-page article in physical order, including all propositions, lemmas, theorems, applications, experiments, and references; separated results proved here from cited background; audited Mathlib and the exact frozen 44-object NumStability surface; and compiled exact private N/L proofs before retaining P45-T1.
annotation.reason: The project owner assigned the P45 source selection and benchmark annotation to Codex.

rejected_candidates.reason: Their minimum-residual and oblique-projection conclusions are short consequences of the displayed inexact Arnoldi relation and do not meet a tier's substantial-proof threshold.
The residual-gap inequalities follow by one finite-sum expansion and the triangle inequality, so they are too easy for T3 and receive no substantial library shortcut.

Lemma 5.2 repeats the same Givens-product argument as Lemma 5.1. The relaxation theorems combine that same coefficient bound with the elementary residual-gap sum, so they do not expose a second distinct substantial NumStability result and cannot serve as no-shortcut T3 tasks.

rejected_candidates.candidate: application propositions in Sections 8-10 and eigenvalue inequalities in Section 11
rejected_candidates.reason: These specialize the same residual-gap/coefficient framework or give direct norm inequalities; they provide neither two independent substantial library shortcuts nor a no-library proof at the required T3 difficulty.
These are numerical experiments rather than universal proof tasks.

T1.decision: Selected the Givens-product core of Lemma 5.1. Exact private proofs show that one substantial NumStability Givens-orthogonality theorem materially shortens L while the complete coefficient bound is absent from both libraries.

T2.decision: Skipped. The paper's complete proved results expose only one qualifying paper-specific substantial shortcut in the frozen bundle, Givens-rotation orthogonality. Generic norm preservation is supporting infrastructure, not a second paper-specific numerical-analysis result.

T3.decision: Skipped. Results independent of the selected Givens argument reduce to short projection, residual-gap, or norm estimates below the T2-level difficulty floor; the harder relaxation results inherit the same NumStability Givens shortcut and therefore fail T3's no-speedup condition.

selection_policy: Use only results and proof steps stated in this paper.
Retain the coefficient conclusion of Lemma 5.1 and expose, rather than assume, the paper's Givens-product norm argument.
Treat generic orthogonal-norm preservation as supporting algebra and the explicit Givens-rotation orthogonality proof as the single substantial shortcut.
Do not count applications of the same coefficient argument as distinct substantial results.
Assign a tier only after exact private N and L proofs compile.
